exact_delta.before: Passed Senate 2026-03-03 (27-0-2, as substituted); received by House and placed on the House 3rd Reading Calendar; circled on 2026-03-06, sent back to House Rules Committee, and killed via 'strike enacting clause'; Senate filed the bill as not passed at 2026-03-06 23:59:59, the close of the 45-day session; it never received a House floor vote
exact_delta.after: Passed Senate 2026-03-03 (27-0-2) after substitution from S1 to S2. House read the bill on its 3rd Reading Calendar and circled it by voice vote 2026-03-06; it returned to House Rules, its enacting clause was struck, and the Senate filed it as not passed late on March6. No House final-passage vote is recorded in the retained history; the procedural voice vote is not bill passage.

exact_delta.before: Energy User Amendments. Earlier versions were described in the prior record as addressing large-load customer property tax and notice issues; the Senate-passed S2 substitute instead addressed eminent-domain limitations relating to energy generation. Filed without enactment.
exact_delta.after: Introduced Energy User Property Tax Amendments proposed statewide distribution of large-load property-tax revenue through population-based county shares, tax-increment agreement restrictions with a pre-May6,2026 agreement exception, and customer-address notice within30days of commission approval of a large-load contract. S1 replaced that program with limits on private pipeline eminent domain serving principally own-use/beneficiary energy generation and a property-owner evidence provision shifting rebuttal to clear-and-convincing proof. Senate-passed S2 omitted the primarily/objective-evidence wording and separate proof-shifting section, and added easement exceptions for pipelines within existing utility easements or immediately adjacent and parallel to existing utility lines; pipelines within or immediately adjacent and parallel to existing/planned roadways; and pipelines able to serve more than one customer on completion. S2 retained prospective/pending-action coverage. These were failed proposals, not current requirements; specific data-center applicability remains unestablished.
